# Board motion: coverage matrix

<!-- Generated by design/tools/board-motion-docs.mjs from design/board-motion/contract/ (coverage.json, cues.json), the prototype fixtures and the proposal manifest of scenes, places and figures. Do not edit by hand. -->

**Approved board-targeting direction; proposed prop/motion/figure adoption.** Issue [#87](https://github.com/Amirkianfar66/GameN/issues/87), board-motion-0.3.0. Design base `94a49ce0c5220b814ec56333b028fbe6180b257e` on `codex/v1-pass-board-targets` ([PR #86](https://github.com/Amirkianfar66/GameN/pull/86), unmerged): protocol 2, engine `full-game-1.1.0`, ruleset `in-person-v1-pass-2026-10-08`, Original Powers off. Tokens 0.4.0, assets `design-0.2.0` plus the scenes and figures `board-motion-0.3.0` (proposal).

Every action of the release is played on the comic board: chosen from a compact tray, its players picked by tapping their characters in their rooms, confirmed and answered in a strip above navigation. Moving is pressing a room's name; Pass is the middle of navigation. This page lists, for each of them, what the viewer's own view offers, how it is drawn, what is public and the cues that mark it; then every cue, the states every one of the nine characters has, the facts the board reads and where each comes from, the components and the runtime hooks they map onto, and the gaps. The reasoning and the integration steps are in [board-motion-handoff.md](board-motion-handoff.md); what was actually run is in [board-motion-verification.md](board-motion-verification.md).

Each scenario id opens in the prototype at `/board-motion/?scenario=<id>` on the design review server (`npm run dev:review --workspace @mothership/design-tokens`). Every name in it is synthetic.
The offer guard checks applicable actor, round, phase, readiness and candidate predicates from the pinned engine and current overlays. It does not prove resources, prior-command history, runoff history or full engine reachability. Since 11 October 2026 five a room is the owner's hard rule (DSN-D27), not yet enforced by the engine (DSN-REQ-12): no fixture offers a full room, and the crowd fixtures, six or more in one room, are layout stress beyond the rule, kept to show the board still draws such a view with everyone reachable. They introduce no adjacency rule.

| Layout stress fixture | Purpose |
| --- | --- |
| `board.crowded` | Layout stress: Seven in Room A, everyone reachable |
| `board.all-one-room` | Layout stress: All nine in Room A |
| `board.crowded-hospital` | Layout stress: Six in the Hospital |
| `board.tightest` | Layout stress: The tallest board: six in Room A, the Captain, two in the Hospital |
| `crowd.shot` | Layout stress: All nine in Room A: a Shot at any of eight |
| `crowd.disable` | Layout stress: All nine in Room A: a Disable at any of eight |
| `crowd.protect` | Layout stress: All nine in Room A: Protection for any of nine |
| `crowd.rescue` | Layout stress: Eight in the Hospital: a Rescue for any of them |
| `crowd.hack` | Layout stress: All nine in Room A: a Hack request with any of eight |
| `crowd.scan` | Layout stress: All nine in Room A: a Scan of any of nine |
| `crowd.supply` | Layout stress: All nine in Room A: Supply, one chosen |
| `crowd.vote` | Layout stress: All nine in Room A: nine candidates, all reachable |

## Every action with every character

An action's rules never look at a character: the view offers seats, and whichever character sits in an offered seat is drawn eligible by the same rules (the check holds the stylesheet to it: a rule keyed by a character sets only its picture). This table says, from the fixtures themselves, in which scenarios each character is offered or chosen for each action; the crowd scenarios put every character the rules allow within reach in one room. A dash is a combination the rules exclude, and the last column says which and why. The vocabulary sheet ([vocabulary.png](../../design/board-motion/review/vocabulary.png)) draws all nine in every state. In these fixtures the viewer is Player 3, character c1.

Pass names no one. Move names a room, never a character: the viewer's own piece is the one that moves, and every character's move is drawn by `cue-public-move`: it gets up from its place, walks, and settles into its new place's gesture (below).

## The states of every character

The states every one of the nine characters has. They are drawn by the same rules for all nine: a character's picture never selects a rule, and nothing about a role or a faction changes any of them. What differs per character is public: its picture. Where it is drawn and in what gesture follows public facts only: its room, the place it holds there, Injured and Eliminated.

| State | Drawn | Cue |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `idle` | The figure at its place in its room, in the place's own gesture (five places a room, each with a gesture of its own; the Command Room's one is the Captain's, at the chart table); in a crowd of six or more, or in the Final Zone, one of three standing stances by seat number. Injured: the same gesture with a bandage; Eliminated: the place's fall. Number and name on a plate under its press area. | none: a state, not a motion |
| `pressed-focused` | A focus outline on the 44 px press area; a light press tint while pressed. | none: a state, not a motion |
| `eligible` | Dashed caption-yellow ring at the base and a + tab; the others faint. | `cue-target-eligible` |
| `selected` | Lifted, solid ring, check stamp. | `cue-selection` |
| `multi-selected` | Solid ring and the pick's number. | `cue-target-pick` |
| `pending` | Dotted ring, ellipsis stamp; the strip's Sending stamp. | `cue-pending` |
| `accepted-registration` | The private marks are gone; the strip carries the Registered stamp. Nothing is drawn on the character. | `cue-registration` |
| `rejected-unavailable` | Faint, without a ring (not offered); a rejection is said in the strip with a hatched stamp, never on the character. | `cue-not-accepted` |
| `authoritative-movement` | Gets up from its place, walks above the board to its new room with an ink trail (limping and bandaged when Injured), and settles into its new place's gesture with a landing puff. The same walk for every character. | `cue-public-move` |
| `public-status-change` | A marker stamped on: Injured (and a bandage at its place), Eliminated (the place's fall, grey, the revealed faction), Captain, Jailed. A health change is first marked by one hit, the same for every cause (cue-public-hit). | `cue-status-change` |
| `active-turn` | The turn marker above the head. | `cue-turn-accent` |

Every character walks, is hit and falls the same way: only its picture differs (fixtures `CREW`, public, never a role).

All nine in all 11 states: [png](../../design/board-motion/review/vocabulary.png).

## Cues

The cues of the board-motion prototype (issue #87): every visible change it animates or marks, what starts it, who may see it, what fact it rests on, where it is drawn, how long, how it is cancelled, what stays when it ends, and what reduced motion shows instead. Six are the reviewed cues of design/contract/motion-cues.json, kept with their ids and durations; the rest are proposals of this work. None is owner-approved.

Rules every cue keeps:

- A cue adds no fact: what it marks is already on screen in words (a status line, a strip line, a tag, the readable list).
- A cue changes nothing and nothing waits for it: no health, resource, turn, phase, deadline or command depends on it. It is never queued.
- Public cues are started only by a change between two drawn public states (seats' location, health, jailed, captain, revealed faction; active seat; phase; round; the published tally). A replayed snapshot, a reconnect, a page that was in the background, and more than four moves in one update play no travel.
- Private cues are drawn only on the acting player's own board while their own action is open, from their own view's offers, their own taps and their own receipts. Closing, a window blur, backgrounding, a stale view, time running out or a new phase removes them.
- No cue exists for a shot, a shooter, a weapon, an attack type, a block, Protection, a Rescue giver, a Supply giver, a Hack partner or any cause, on any surface. A health change is drawn the same whatever caused it.
- No cue has a sound, a vibration pattern, a light change in a room or a fetched picture. All pictures are in the bundles every device loads before the first view.
- Cue layers take no pointer events and cannot take focus. A newer authoritative state withdraws the cue in flight for the same seat; the latest state is what is drawn.
- Reduced motion: no travel, trail, shake, lift or zoom. Arrival, status changes, stamps and sheets use the 80 ms fade. The facts and the controls are the same.

## Facts and where they come from

Every fact the board draws, the authorized source it is read from at the pinned tuple, who may see it and the cues that draw it. Nothing is drawn from anything else. A place (where in a room a character is drawn, and so its gesture) is not a game fact: every device works it out the same way from public occupancy, seat order and the places drawn before (design/board-motion/js/layout.js).

| Fact | Drawn | Source at the pinned tuple | Audience | Cues |

| `seat-identity` | Each character's picture, seat number and name on its plate. | Lobby identity: seats[].characterId and seats[].displayName (packages/contracts/src/lobby-identity.ts), as the release's comic shell already reads them; seat numbers from seatId. | public | — |
| `location` | The room a character is in, and its place there. | seats[].location in the public and player views (packages/contracts/src/full-game.ts); PUBLIC_MOVE events. | public | `cue-public-move` `layout-reflow` |
| `health` | Injured (a bandage at its place, a limp when it walks, the marker) and Eliminated (the place's fall, grey, the marker). One hit, the same for every cause, marks the change. | seats[].health; PUBLIC_HEALTH_CHANGED events (new health only, no cause). | public | `cue-public-hit` `cue-status-change` |
| `jailed` | The Jailed marker. | seats[].jailed (views only: no event of its own; a change is seen as the difference between two views). | public | `cue-status-change` |
| `captain` | The Captain marker. | seats[].captain (views only). | public | `cue-status-change` |
| `revealed-faction` | The faction label on an Eliminated character. | seats[].revealedFaction, which the contract sets only for Eliminated seats before the end. | public | `cue-status-change` |

## Rooms, places and gestures

The owner's decision of 9 October 2026: each room is a scene with five fixed places, each with a gesture of its own, the Command Room one (the Captain's); 21 places in all. Who takes which place is worked out on every device from public facts only (`design/board-motion/js/layout.js`): the Captain takes the chart table; elsewhere the places are a function of who is in the room now, the same on every screen and after a reconnect: the lowest seat first, each takes the first free place in its own order of preference, seat `n` first at place `(n - 1) mod 5`, so the higher seat of a pair steps to its next place when the lower one comes in. An Injured character keeps its gesture and wears a bandage; an Eliminated one takes the place's fall. The places are drawn, not enforced: six to nine in one room stand in a 3 x 3 crowd (layout stress) in one of three stances by seat number, as in the Final Zone. No capacity is implied: see GAP-2.

## The two animations of every gesture

Every gesture has the owner's two animations, generated from it by the figure rig (`design/board-motion/figures/motion.mjs`) rather than drawn frame by frame, so a new place's gesture has them at once. Both are public, both belong to a public fact, both are the same for every character, and both have a reduced-motion form with no travel, jolt or fall.

| Animation | Fact | What is drawn | Timing | Cue |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Moving to another room | A PUBLIC_MOVE: the seat is in another location | Gets up from the place's gesture (the old room keeps an echo of it), walks above the board from its feet there to its feet at the new place with an ink trail, settles into the new place's gesture with a landing puff. Injured, it limps and wears its bandage. | 120 / 450 / 330 ms (motionBeatsMs.pieceMove) | `cue-public-move` |
| Hit, Injured | PUBLIC_HEALTH_CHANGED to Injured, nothing else | A burst at the chest and a jolt of the gesture (both at 80 ms), a flinch, back into the gesture with a bandage. If the same update moves it (the Hospital at the end of the round), it walks out hurt and limps there. | 320 ms impact (motionMs.publicImpact), settled by 720 ms | `cue-public-hit` |
| Hit, Eliminated | PUBLIC_HEALTH_CHANGED to Eliminated, nothing else | The same burst and jolt, then the fall into the place's fall: slumped over the desk or the bench, or down on the deck. Grey, with the marker and the faction the rules reveal. | 240 / 260 / 400 ms (motionBeatsMs.comicBeatMaximum) | `cue-public-hit` |

No shot, shooter, weapon, trajectory or direction is drawn: a public view says only that a health changed (GAP-9).

| `tray` | `section.bm-tray > button.bm-chip[data-act=open:<kind>]` | `the Actions view: [data-intent=action/open][data-kind] in .ms-offers (data-phone-view=actions)` | extend | private | A compact two-column tray over the lower board with only the actions the viewer's view opens; Move is not in it. |
| `nav` | `nav.bm-nav > button#bm-pass.bm-pass[data-act=pass]` | `.phone-nav[data-region=phone-navigation] > button#ms-phone-pass.phone-pass[data-intent=action/pass]` | reuse | public | Board, Actions, Pass in the middle, Card, Menu. Pass is drawn the same on every phone; it is available only on the viewer's own ordinary turn and absent in legacy matches. |
| `status` | `header.bm-status > .bm-status__round, .bm-status__line, .bm-timer[role=timer]` | `.ms-phase__labels[data-region=phase], .ms-timer[data-region=timer]` | reuse | public | Round, phase or whose turn, and the timer. Its size never changes. |
| `result-sheet` | `section.bm-result[data-ended=finished\|aborted][data-winner] > .bm-result__outcome, .bm-result__line, table.bm-cast > tr.bm-cast__row[data-seat][data-end-faction][data-code], .bm-result__code` | `div.ms-result-region[data-region=result] > section.ms-panel.ms-result (renderResult in parts.ts): #ms-result-heading, .ms-result__outcome, .ms-result__line, table.ms-result__roles > tr[data-seat]` | extend | public | The match's end over the lower board, on every phone and the shared display alike, in the release's words: the winner struck on a ribbon in its side's colour, the Alien's co-win, the release's table of roles drawn as a cast list in two columns (each seat's character, its label, its role in its side's colour, the Code's four pinned) and the Code's sentence; a match the host ended shows its sentence only. Hidden behind the menu, as the release hides its result there. |
| `connection-banner` | `div.bm-banner[data-variant=stale\|unreadable] > .bm-banner__icon, .bm-banner__text, button.bm-banner__act[data-act=reconnect]` | `div.ms-banner.ms-banner--connection[data-variant] (renderBanner in parts.ts, buildBanners in common.ts) with #ms-banner-connection-action[data-intent=session/reconnect]` | extend | local | The view may be out of date: the connection is lost, or the latest update could not be read. The release's words and its one control, Reconnect now, with the reviewed stale-connection icon, over the top of the board. Every open sheet keeps clear of it (--bm-banner-clear), so that its heading and Close stay in view on a short phone. Its change is said once in the public live region, as the release's announcements say it; nothing plays. |

## Gaps and open decisions

What this design needs that the pinned tuple does not provide, and what it deliberately does not draw. None is a contract change made here: Integration owns the contracts.

| Id | Kind | What | In this design |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| GAP-1 | none needed | Jailed, Captain and revealed-faction changes have no event of their own. | Draw them from the difference between two drawn views, as the release's director does for health and location. No contract change is proposed. |
| GAP-2 | owner decision | The owner's reference asked for at most five players in a room; on 9 October 2026 the owner said “lets say the maximum capacity of each room is 5”, and on 11 October 2026 “yes enforce 5 as a hard rule”, deciding its six cases the same day (“yes go with your recommendations for all six”). The rules and the engine have no room capacity yet: rules/overlays/location-board-layout-v1.json says "Unnumbered token areas avoid imposing an artificial room-capacity rule", and the server's starting rooms are an independent coin flip for each player (issue #83). | Five fixed places a room, each with its own gesture (the Command Room one, the Captain's), a character keeping its place while it stays; the Eliminated count. A full room says FULL on its tag, on every screen, from public occupancy: Room A and Room B, never offered when full, and the Hospital and the Jail, where a full Hospital is why an Injured character waits in its room. No fixture offers a full room. The engine is to enforce the rule and its six cases (DSN-D27, DSN-REQ-12, issue #96, Backend, with Balance's audit); until it does, a view with six to nine in one room is still drawn, as a 3 x 3 crowd in which everyone can be pressed (layout stress). |
| GAP-3 | owner decision | The reference draws arrows and lights along a corridor between rooms. The rules give no adjacency: rules/overlays/location-board-layout-v1.json says its dotted paths "illustrate possible Captain access, not a finalized adjacency decision". | A steel spine with four lamps between the columns, no arrow, door or path. |
| GAP-4 | owner decision | Room subtitles (Captain, Engineering, Laboratory) come from the reference, not from the rules or the release. | Proposed words, aria-hidden; the room's name is what is read and pressed. |
| GAP-5 | asset | The five room scenes (each approved room around a new deck, the props of its places and its light, and the layers drawn in front of a place: the chart table, the laboratory bench, the two beds) are not in the reviewed manifest design-0.2.0. | Built from the approved sources, their groups lifted unchanged and printed by the reviewed export recipes, as a versioned proposal (board-motion-0.3.0, one public stylesheet loaded before the first match view); adopted only through an Integration review of a later manifest revision (DSN-D30). |
| GAP-6 | asset | The Final Zone has no picture of its own in the reviewed kit. | The page's paper ground with the approved halftone and speed lines. A picture is a later asset decision. |
| GAP-7 | asset | The full-body figures (the nine characters in 27 gestures: 21 places, three crowd stances, three falls; and a move and a hit from every gesture; owner's decisions of 9 October 2026) are not in the reviewed manifest design-0.2.0, and the runtime still draws the approved bust standees. | Drawn live by one rig in design/board-motion/figures/ after the approved standees, in their own colors, as a versioned proposal (board-motion-0.3.0): no figure art is fetched; the sheets of every gesture are written on request for review. Adopting them is an Integration step and drawing them the game Frontend's (DSN-D32). |
| GAP-8 | owner decision | design/contract/crew-catalog.json says a character never changes with health, Jail, the Captain or anything private, and that those are markers on the piece. A figure's gesture follows public facts: the place it holds in its room, the Captain at the chart table, a bandage when Injured, the place's fall when Eliminated. | The character (face, skin, hair, colors, suit) never changes; only the gesture does, from public facts only, and every marker is still drawn. Whether a gesture may say what a marker says is for the game owner, with Integration for the catalog (DSN-D33). |
| GAP-9 | owner decision | The owner asked for an animation “if got shot” for every gesture. A public view says only that a health changed, never that a shot was fired, by whom, with what or from where (a Disable and a showdown shot also deal damage). The reviewed motion contract accepts “a health change is a status change with no impact”, and motion-direction.md allows a burst only when the attack type is public. | One hit for every cause (cue-public-hit, a proposal): a burst and a jolt where the character is, then a flinch back into its gesture with a bandage (Injured) or the place's fall (Eliminated). No lettering, weapon, shooter, trajectory or direction. Drawing a shot as a shot needs a public shot fact: a rules and contract decision (DSN-D35). |

## Scenes and figures

Public art for the board-motion prototype (the owner's decisions of 9 October 2026): the five rooms as scenes with fixed places, built around the approved rooms, and the nine characters as full-body figures drawn by a rig in a gesture for every place. The reviewed manifest and bundles are unchanged; this art is proposed for a later export revision and is adopted only through Integration. Rights: Scenes: the approved rooms' groups copied element for element from the repository's original vector sources under design/source/board/, recolored by the reviewed export recipes, around new vector drawing generated for this repository by design/board-motion/scenes/. Figures: original vector drawings generated for this repository by design/board-motion/figures/, after the approved standees under design/source/crew/ and in their colors (design tokens 0.4.0). No third-party artwork, font, photograph, traced image or generated raster image. Use inside the Mothership project only. Any other use needs the game owner's decision (DSN-D06).

Every device, with the public-board bundle, before the first match view, whatever the seat's role, state or turn. Contains public art only. One stylesheet, `design/board-motion/assets/board-motion.scenes.css`, 118127 bytes.
